article_title: Increasing Undergraduate Success: A Randomized Controlled Trial of "U-Pace" Instruction
citation: Fleming, R., Pedrick, L.E., Soiber, L., Kienzler, S., Fleming, R.R., & Reddy, D.M. (2018). Increasing undergraduate success: A randomized controlled trial of U-Pace instruction. Online Learning, 22(3), 175-191. https://doi.org/10.24059/olj.v22i3.1317
title: U-Pace instruction: an online instructional model integrating concept mastery and amplified assistance
description: U-Pace instruction is an online instructional model comprising two empirically supported components: concept mastery and amplified assistance. In concept mastery, "students typically master one content unit before progressing to a new content unit"; in U-Pace, students must score at least 90% on each unit quiz before advancing. Amplified assistance is "personalized support provided by the instructor to all students without them having to ask for help", delivered as weekly instructor-initiated email tailored from learning management system data. The RCT reported here found the combination, not either component alone, produced greater learning.
requirements: Instructors trained to implement the conditions with fidelity, following an implementation manual
Learning management system information about student engagement and performance available to instructors for tailoring assistance
Field-tested U-Pace templates for crafting support messages
constraints: Evaluated in a single course context (Introduction to Psychology), a limitation the authors state
Grades are determined differently in mastery versus nonmastery approaches, which the authors note as a limitation
target_learners: Undergraduates in gateway courses, including students at risk for college noncompletion
target_learning_goals: Academic success (final grades of A or B)
Learning measured independently of grades on a proctored cumulative exam
examples: In the RCT, U-Pace students worked through 24 content units, retaking quizzes with different questions after at least an hour, while receiving weekly personalized support emails

article_title: Increasing Undergraduate Success: A Randomized Controlled Trial of "U-Pace" Instruction
citation: Fleming, R., Pedrick, L.E., Soiber, L., Kienzler, S., Fleming, R.R., & Reddy, D.M. (2018). Increasing undergraduate success: A randomized controlled trial of U-Pace instruction. Online Learning, 22(3), 175-191. https://doi.org/10.24059/olj.v22i3.1317
title: Field-tested U-Pace email templates for amplified assistance messages
description: The U-Pace instructors used "freely available, field-tested U-Pace templates" to craft proactive, personalized email support messages. The templates specified that messages should contain "help with concepts not yet mastered, behavior-based praise to shape student performance toward success, and elements to modify students' beliefs that they could be successful even if they were unsuccessful at the moment". Instructors tailored messages using time elapsed since the last quiz attempt and quiz scores from the learning management system.
requirements: Instructor access to learning management system data on student engagement and performance
Instructors trained to tailor messages in response to inferred student needs
constraints: Messages were evaluated for alignment with templates in this study's fidelity checks; effectiveness of templates alone was not separately tested
target_learners: Undergraduate students in online gateway courses
target_learning_goals: Sustained engagement and motivation toward mastering course content
Modified student beliefs about themselves as learners
examples: Fidelity checks every two weeks confirmed all U-Pace and amplified assistance students received instructor-initiated weekly support messages aligned with the templates
